extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent practitioners, inventors, and USPTO examiners
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for applying U.S. inventorship law to inventions for which AI systems (including generative AI and computational models) were used in the inventive process; clarifies how existing statutory and case-law standards govern naming inventors. Intended to inform applicants, prosecutors, and examiners about what counts as inventorship when AI is involved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uniform legal standard applies regardless of AI use
rubrics_metrics.description: The same legal standard for determining inventorship applies to all inventions, regardless of whether AI systems were used in the inventive process. No new, separate or modified standard is created for or applies to AI-assisted inventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating inventorship, apply existing statutory and case-law tests the same way for AI-assisted inventions as for traditionally developed inventions; do not create special rules or categories because AI was used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Only natural persons can be named as inventors
rubrics_metrics.description: A hallmark of U.S. law is that only natural persons can be properly named as inventors on patent applications. "'[I]nventor' means the individual . . . who invented or discovered the subject matter of the invention." 35 U.S.C. § 100(f).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not list AI systems, software, companies, or other non-human entities as inventors. Named inventors must be human individuals consistent with the statutory definition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventorship based on conception
rubrics_metrics.description: The "'invention' in the Patent Act unquestionably refers to the inventor’s conception." Pfaff v. Wells Elecs., Inc., 525 U.S. 55, 60 (1988).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inventorship determinations center on which individual(s) conceived the claimed invention (i.e., formed the definite and permanent idea of the invention), applying established conception-law principles rather than relying on the role of tools or assistance.

rubrics_metrics.name: USPTO presumption that named inventors are the actual human inventors
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO presumes that the inventors named on the application data sheet or oath/declaration are the actual, human-being inventors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unless evidence suggests otherwise, the USPTO will treat the persons named in the application as the inventors. Challenges to inventorship should supply countervailing evidence to overcome this presumption.

rubrics_metrics.name: AI systems are tools and do not qualify as inventors
rubrics_metrics.description: AI systems, including generative AI and other computational models, are tools used by human inventors. Like any tool, while AI systems may assist inventors, such tools do not qualify for or elevate such assistance to inventor status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When inventors used AI in the inventive process, analyze the human contributors' conception and contributions; the mere involvement of AI does not create inventorship for the AI or change how human contribution is evaluated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy alignment with Executive Order 14179
rubrics_metrics.description: The new guidance implements Executive Order 14179 of January 23, 2025 ("Removing Barriers to American Leadership in Artificial Intelligence"), which directs agencies to review and revise policies established under the prior administration to ensure they promote American leadership in AI.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USPTO policy on inventorship for AI-assisted inventions has been revised to align with the Executive Order's direction to reassess prior policies; practitioners should expect USPTO rules and public guidance to reflect that objective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rescission of prior (February 2024) guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO published revised inventorship guidance for AI-assisted inventions, rescinding its February 2024 guidance on this topic in its entirety.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practitioners should no longer rely on the February 2024 guidance and should follow the revised guidance as the controlling USPTO position on inventorship when AI tools were used.
